extra.message: The /portal-entry endpoint is anonymous (@Secured(IS_ANONYMOUS)) and logs a user in based solely on an attacker-controlled cookie 'campus_directory_id'. There is no signature, token, or shared-secret verification tying this cookie to the actual campus portal — any client can set this cookie to an arbitrary email address and be authenticated as that user (including an admin/instructor account) without a password.

/portal-assertion parses the JWT via SignedJWT.parse(body.get("assertion")), which only decodes the token — it never calls verify(JWSVerifier) to check the signature. An attacker can craft an arbitrary unsigned/garbage-signature JWT with any 'sub' claim and be logged in as that user, a complete authentication bypass.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: User-supplied 'message' field from the JSON body is concatenated directly into an HTML response without any escaping, and the endpoint is anonymous. This allows reflected XSS.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS)

extra.message: The 'label' field from the request body (user-controlled, defaults to a safe value but can be overridden freely) is concatenated directly into a shell command string executed via new ProcessBuilder("sh","-c", command). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `; rm -rf /` or `$(...)`) in the label field to execute arbitrary OS commands.

courseArtwork fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL (assetUrl query parameter) server-side via HttpClient with no allow-list/host validation, enabling SSRF against internal services (e.g. cloud metadata endpoints, internal admin panels) from the application server.

retrieveBrief fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL (briefSource query parameter, reachable by any instructor/TA) server-side via HttpClient with no host allow-list, enabling SSRF against internal network resources.

exportSectionRosterCsv builds a SQL query by directly concatenating the caller-supplied 'sectionCode' (from the X-Course-Code header in AdminController.exportSectionRoster) into the SQL string executed via Statement.executeQuery, with no parameterization. This allows classic SQL injection.

The 'edulms_plan_basket' cookie value, fully attacker-controlled, is base64-decoded and deserialized with raw java.io.ObjectInputStream.readObject(). Native Java deserialization of untrusted data is a well-known remote code execution vector via gadget chains present on the classpath.

The 'edulms_grade_queue' cookie value is base64-decoded and passed into a bare, unhardened com.thoughtworks.xstream.XStream().fromXML(). XStream without a configured security framework/type permissions is vulnerable to remote code execution via gadget chains when fed attacker-controlled XML.

formulaPreview compiles and executes an attacker-supplied MVEL expression (query parameter 'expression') via org.mvel2.MVEL.executeExpression with no sandboxing. MVEL expressions can invoke arbitrary Java methods, resulting in remote code execution.

conditionPreview evaluates an attacker-supplied BeanShell expression (body field 'condition') via javax.script ScriptEngine ('bsh') with no sandboxing. BeanShell scripts can execute arbitrary Java code, resulting in remote code execution.

renderMaterial builds a command string with the attacker-controlled 'outputFormat' body field concatenated in, then runs it via new ProcessBuilder("cmd","/c", command) which lets cmd.exe interpret the full string. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '&', '|') into outputFormat to run arbitrary OS commands.

renderNotice compiles and processes the entire caller-supplied body (from AdminController.previewNotice's X-Notice-Body header) as a FreeMarker template with new freemarker.template.Template. FreeMarker templates can invoke arbitrary Java via built-ins/statics, so this is server-side template injection leading to remote code execution.

renderReplyStencil evaluates the attacker-controlled 'stencil' cookie value ('edulms_reply_stencil') as an Apache Velocity template via Velocity.evaluate with no restricted context. Velocity templates can invoke arbitrary Java methods on context objects, leading to server-side template injection and remote code execution.

partnerCatalogSelection builds an XPath expression by directly concatenating 'section', which originates from the attacker-controlled 'edulms_campus_section' cookie read in PartnerController.campusCatalog, with no escaping. This allows XPath injection to alter the query logic (e.g. break out of the @code='...' predicate).

reconcileCatalogRequests builds an XPath expression by concatenating each uploaded line ('code') directly into the query string without escaping, allowing XPath injection via a crafted catalogue-request upload.

importRoster builds an LDAP search filter by concatenating the uploaded 'campusId' value directly into the filter string ('(&(objectClass=person)(uid=' + campusId + '))'), with no escaping of LDAP special characters. An attacker who controls the uploaded roster file can inject LDAP filter syntax to alter the search.

learnerSummary reflects the request's Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows any origin to make authenticated cross-origin requests and read the response, letting a malicious website exfiltrate a logged-in user's enrollment/profile data.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: This filter applies to every route ('/**') and, for ANY request carrying an 'embed' query parameter, strips X-Frame-Options/CSP and replaces them with X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL and frame-ancestors *. Because it is driven purely by an unauthenticated, attacker-controllable query string on any URL (including authenticated pages), any attacker can frame any page of the application — including admin/instructor pages reached by a logged-in victim — by appending ?embed=1 to a link, enabling clickjacking attacks.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: On every application startup, an H2 web console is launched with '-webAllowOthers', binding it to all network interfaces on port 8082 with no authentication configured. The H2 console permits arbitrary SQL execution and, via CREATE ALIAS, arbitrary Java code execution, so any network-reachable attacker can gain full database and potential host compromise.

importSchedule parses the uploaded term-schedule file with the default (unsafe) org.yaml.snakeyaml.Yaml().load(), which can instantiate arbitrary Java types from YAML tags. Depending on classpath gadgets this can lead to remote code execution from an uploaded YAML file.

exportRosterCsv, when 'withAccountCols' is true, writes each student's raw BCrypt password hash (s.getPasswordHash()) and password-reset token (s.getResetToken()) into the exported CSV. Exposing password hashes and live reset tokens in an exportable report is sensitive-data exposure that enables offline password cracking or account takeover via the leaked reset token.

The datasource configuration falls back to a hardcoded default password ('edulms_dev_pw') and username when the JDBC_PASSWORD/JDBC_USER environment variables are not set, and the same literal is duplicated in docker-compose.yml. If deployed without overriding these environment variables, the database is protected by a credential that is public in source control.
